title: Class thickness adds held-out BATS oxygen skill beyond annual winter ventilation and depth in 1989-2025
abstract: Does local class thickness add to annual-forced ventilation after model amplitude and depth are fitted? We combine published BATS annual aggregates and 89 age-consistent model sets on sigma0 26.5. In blocked tests with two-year buffers, thickness lowers primary AOU error from 4.05 to 2.72 umol/kg. The mean squared-error gain is 8.99, with a conditional block interval of 1.80 to 15.13. All 89 sets improve; the year-to-year thickness slope also stays negative. Processing checks and conditional phase controls retain the result. But geometry alone gives blocked error of 2.65, and only 12 sets beat it. An early-fit test favors the combined model. Thus thickness supplies useful information about the missing response, but these data do not identify a separate class-volume cause or respiration change. Limits include 37 years at one station, shared bottles for geometry and AOU, retrospective design, and conditional uncertainty. No projection is made.
